title: Count the years?
text: The cheer squad wants this week's banner to count the years since the club's last premiership. Half the members love it; the other half think the Saints have been reminded enough. They've asked the coach.

choices.label: Put it up: we're the ones who'll end it

effects.why: The group knows what a flag would mean down here

choices.result: The count is on the banner. It adds weight to a tight game.

choices.label: Leave the count off and paint the club, not the wait
choices.result: The players run out free. The old hands feel the history is being hidden.

title: Spoon talk
text: The side is down at the bottom, and the papers have run a graphic of every wooden spoon in the club's history. It's a long list, and the players have seen it pinned up in the café across the road.

choices.label: Front it: that's our history, not our future
choices.result: The group feels protected. The story lives another week.

choices.label: Ban the papers from the rooms

effects.why: The group's focus stayed inside the club

hit.why: The leaders felt treated like kids

effects.hit_result: The leaders feel treated like kids.

choices.result: No papers in the rooms this week.

choices.label: Put the graphic on the whiteboard

effects.hit_result: The group bites. They want to wipe it off.
effects.miss_result: Some of them sink. It's too much to carry.

choices.result: The list of spoons is up on the board.

title: Strength Through Loyalty
text: {name} is out of contract and wants one more year. He's a club man to his bootstraps and the room adores him, but his legs are going and the list needs the spot for a kid. The members are already quoting the motto on the crest at you.

choices.label: Give him one more year

effects.why: The room saw loyalty repaid

choices.result: {first} goes around again. A kid waits another year for the spot.

choices.label: Thank him and let him go with a send-off
choices.result: {first} leaves on his own terms. Some of the senior group wonder if they're next.

choices.label: Offer him a coaching role instead

effects.why: A club man stayed in the building
He wanted to keep playing

effects.hit_result: He wanted to play. He signs elsewhere as a player.

choices.result: The offer is on the table for {first}.

title: Moorabbin or the highway
text: The rooms at Moorabbin are tired, and the board has two offers: spend big to rebuild the old ground, or take a council deal for a new base further down the peninsula. The members see Moorabbin as home.

choices.label: Rebuild Moorabbin

effects.why: Moorabbin stays home for the members

choices.result: The heartland is thrilled. The works get in the way of training.

choices.label: Move down the highway

effects.hit_result: The new base turns sour, and the board regrets the move.

choices.result: Modern facilities, sooner. The supporters feel the club has left them.

choices.label: Patch it up and wait
choices.result: No money spent. The players notice the cold showers.

title: Back to the Junction
text: The heritage committee wants the players to train one morning at the Junction Oval, the club's old home, with the old-timers lining the fence. It falls in a short week.

choices.label: Go: a light session at the Junction

effects.why: The group learned where the club came from

choices.result: The old-timers line the fence. The session is lighter in a short week.

choices.label: Not this week; send the leaders to a lunch
choices.result: Main training goes ahead. The heritage committee feels brushed off.

title: Beside the seaside
text: The history group wants the club's old run-out song, I Do Like To Be Beside The Seaside, played as the side runs out at a home game. Some of the players have never heard it.

choices.label: Play it, and teach the players the story

effects.why: The group learned the old run-out song

choices.result: The old members are moved. It's a distraction in game week.

choices.label: Keep the run-out as it is

effects.why: Game day routine stayed the same

choices.result: No change to the routine. The history group goes to the papers.

title: Sand at Sandringham
text: The fitness staff want a session on the beach at Sandringham, then a hit-out on the beach oval next door. The sand builds legs, but it's a hard week to do it.

choices.label: Beach session, full tilt
choices.result: A tougher, fitter side for the back half of the year. Tired legs this weekend.

choices.label: A light walk in the water
choices.result: The players recover and have a laugh. Little fitness gained.

choices.label: Stay at Moorabbin
choices.result: Normal routine. The same track every day, and the group goes a bit flat.

title: The bayside heartland
text: The membership team has money for one big campaign. Saints supporters are packed into the bayside suburbs tighter than any other Melbourne club's. Dig deeper there, or chase new fans elsewhere?

choices.label: Dig in: bayside and the peninsula

effects.hit_result: Safe, loyal growth. The heartland signs up.
effects.miss_result: The heartland is already signed up. There was nowhere left to grow.

choices.result: The campaign stays close to home.

choices.label: Chase the growth corridors in the south-east

effects.hit_result: It works. A new generation of Saints signs up.
effects.miss_result: New fans are fickle in a lean year. The money is gone.

choices.result: The campaign heads out to the new suburbs.

title: A home game across the water
text: A city interstate or across the Tasman has offered serious money to host one of the Saints' home games every year. The board likes the cheque; the members hate losing a game.

choices.label: Take the deal

effects.why: The members lost a home game

choices.result: A big boost to the books. The side travels for a home game.

choices.label: Turn it down

effects.why: The members kept every home game

choices.result: The members keep every home game. The board loses its cheque.

choices.label: Take it for one year only

effects.why: The members still grumble about the trip

choices.result: Cash now, and a trial. The members still grumble.

title: The stadium deal
text: The crowds at home are healthy, but the ground deal leaves the club little at the gate. The board wants to shift a home game to the 'G, where the Saints take home more.

choices.label: Move one game to the 'G
choices.result: Better gate takings. A bigger, less familiar ground for that game.

choices.label: Stay where we are
choices.result: The players know every blade of grass. The books stay tight.

title: The local kid
text: A kid from the local under-18 side, who has trained at Moorabbin since he was fifteen, grew up in a Saints scarf. The recruiters rate him, but not as highly as another player who'll be there at your pick.

choices.label: Take the local kid

effects.why: The pick went to the local kid, not the higher ceiling

choices.result: The members love it. He'd run through a wall for the club.

choices.label: Take the best available

effects.why: The club took the higher ceiling

choices.result: The higher ceiling. The heartland grumbles about another one that got away.

title: Our own reserves, or a partner?
text: The club's partnership with a local state-league club is up for renewal. Going alone costs more but gives your coaches full control of the reserves; staying aligned keeps a proud local club alive and the bills down.

choices.label: Stay aligned
choices.result: Cheaper, and good local ties. The fringe players get fewer minutes in your system.

choices.label: Run our own reserves side
choices.result: Full control of development. It's dearer, and the local club is hurt.

title: So close, again
text: The season is over, and the rooms are silent. The club's history is full of years like this one. The coach has to set the tone for the summer.

choices.label: Remember this feeling and bring it back next year

effects.why: The group carried the hurt into the summer

effects.hit_result: Some of them can't let it go.

choices.result: The hunger carries into the pre-season.

choices.label: Close the book: rest, then start fresh

effects.why: The hurt was put away, not used

choices.result: The players recover in body and mind. The edge may dull.

choices.label: Front a full review with the board
choices.result: The board sees accountability. The players feel picked over.

title: Saved from the creditors
text: The debt has crept up, and a wealthy Saints man has offered to lead a rescue if he can take the chair. He gets things done, but he'll want a say in the football department too.

choices.label: Back his takeover

effects.hit_result: The new president loses patience and starts leaning on the coach.

choices.result: The debts are sorted fast. A new president has your number.

choices.label: Run a members' appeal instead

effects.why: The club stayed the members' own

effects.hit_result: The members dig deep. The debt comes down.
effects.miss_result: The appeal falls short, and the board wanted it done faster.

choices.result: The club asks its own people for help.

choices.label: Cut the football budget
choices.result: No outside hands on the club. The players feel the cuts.

title: The rebel ticket
text: After a lean stretch, a group of former players and big members has launched a ticket to spill the board. They want the coach's public backing.

choices.label: Back the current board

effects.hit_result: The rebels win. You start on the outer.

choices.result: The people paying you remember your loyalty.

choices.label: Back the rebels

effects.hit_result: The rebels win, and the new board owes you.
effects.miss_result: The rebels lose, and the old board remembers.

choices.result: You've picked a side in public.

choices.label: Say you coach and the members vote

effects.why: The coach stayed above the boardroom fight

choices.result: Above the fight. Neither side owes you anything.

title: Nights on Fitzroy Street
text: Photos have surfaced of a group of Saints players out late on Fitzroy Street in a game week. Nothing illegal, but the papers love it, and the club's name is in every headline.

choices.label: Fine them and drop the worst offender

effects.why: The club made its standards clear

choices.result: One fewer good player this weekend. The group is split.

choices.label: Deal with it in-house

effects.why: The group closed ranks

effects.hit_result: The papers keep digging, and the board loses patience.

choices.result: The group closes ranks. The press says the club's soft.

choices.label: Ban the strip in game weeks for everyone

effects.why: One rule for the whole list

choices.result: One rule for all. The players who did nothing feel punished.

title: The culture review
text: A string of off-field incidents has the club in the news for the wrong reasons. The board has ordered an outside review of the club's culture and wants the coach to lead it from inside.

choices.label: Open the doors to the reviewers

effects.why: The club faced its review in the open

choices.result: A clean slate, and the public sees it. Weeks of interviews and leaks.

choices.label: Keep it small and quiet

effects.hit_result: It leaks, and it looks like a cover-up.

choices.result: Less noise around the players.

title: Marching in after the siren
text: After a big win, the players want to stay out and sing the song with the cheer squad in the forward pocket. The recovery staff want them in the ice baths.

choices.label: Sing with the fans

effects.hit_result: Recovery runs late, and the legs are heavy next week.

choices.result: A night the supporters won't forget.

choices.label: Song in the rooms, then recovery
choices.result: The routine holds. The fans see the backs of the players.

effects.hit_result: The old boys get through to him. He stays happy.

text: It's Collingwood this week, and the old Saints love nothing more. A club great who played in some of the big Saints and Pies games offers to speak to the group on Thursday night.

choices.label: Keep it a normal week
choices.result: A calm build-up. The old players feel shut out.

title: Everyone's welcome

choices.label: Lead it, with the players front and centre

text: The club is staging a match to raise money and talk openly about mental health, in honour of a much-loved club great. The players have been asked to share their own stories with the press during the week.
